title: Hosted API: triage, hotfix, and progressive soft-throttle for recurring 5xx waves
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
Multiple customers reported sudden spikes of 5xx and long tail timeouts over the last 48 hours. These escalate to customer P0s because retries amplify load and push the serving tier into a degraded state. This ticket owns triage, an emergency hotfix to stop amplification, and a progressive soft-throttle feature to absorb tenant surges without hard-failing requests.

Scope:
- Immediate mitigation to prevent retry amplification and connection pool exhaustion in Hosted API.
- Short-term hotfix rollout to edge/proxy and serving runtime.
- Progressive rollout of tenant-scoped soft-throttle and HC/queue admission controls.
- Postmortem and follow-up reliability engineering work to remove root causes.

Primary affected surfaces: hosted inference API (text-generation/chat), edge proxy connection pools, runtime KV cache compaction path.
root_cause: Initial investigation shows a confluence of factors: a) periodic KV cache compaction triggered at ~95% memory watermark causing a spike of longer tail requests, b) edge connection pool admission not backpressuring fast enough which allowed many slow requests to tie up worker slots, and c) client SDK retries (default exponential) causing request amplification. The combination produced tenant-local surge waves and cascading 5xx timeouts from overwhelmed workers.
mitigation: 1) Deploy an edge-level soft-throttle that returns 429 with Retry-After under controlled thresholds for affected tenants to prevent worker saturation. 2) Patch runtime to reduce synchronous KV compaction pauses (stream compaction mode) and add a small jitter. 3) Adjust proxy connection pool to prefer fast failures on queuing beyond threshold. 4) Temporary customer comms recommending SDK retry backoff tuning for impacted tenants.
rollback_plan: Hotfixes will be gated by canary: deploy to canary region (10% of traffic) with automated verification. If canary shows >5% regression of success rate or unexplained latency increase, rollback proxy change first, then runtime change. All rollbacks executable via existing terraform-blue/green playbook within 20 minutes.
verification_criteria:
- Canary success: error rate reduction >=50% for target tenants and no >10% latency regression.
- Dashboards: per-tenant 5xx drops, connection pool saturation under control, lower retry amplification metric (requests-per-origin over baseline).
- Synthetic checks: 1k/sec synthetic generation across sequence length distribution with stable tail latency (p95/p99 within SLAs).
